The finite-grid canonical gravity candidate needs a controlled nonlinear evolution after exact full-zone closure fails in the fixed local class. This unit gives an explicit alternative: a supplied nonlinear gravity/scalar Hamiltonian with finite-order alias-free brackets, uniform analytic-time evolution, and convergent sampled constraints. The spectral version has exponentially small analytic sampling error; the actual centered finite-range law has an O(epsilon²) approximation theorem. The derivative, carrier and analytic-data assumptions are explicit.

The note includes the coupled scalar variation, all claimed bracket/Jacobi obligations as analytic arguments, constraint propagation and a nonconstant compatible-data construction. The all-zone spatial-bracket defect remains visible. The numerical runs corroborate formulas and actual trajectories; they do not prove the universal bounds or compute nested Jacobi.
